objective: Move release approval decisions into the complete release-application business detail while keeping workflow as the authoritative task, permission, signature and audit platform.
users: approvers entering from dashboard, task center, notification or H5 links
release applicants reviewing form details and workflow progress
workflow administrators configuring and monitoring processes

requirements.statement: The release business detail owns the approval interface.
acceptance: Full application context and current-task actions render on one page
counterexample: Approval can be submitted from a generic workflow dialog without release details

requirements.statement: All release detail and approval entries use one stable business route.
acceptance: Application list, inbox, done, notification and H5 resolve to /release/applications/:applicationCode

requirements.statement: Dashboard and task center aggregate and navigate but never approve.
acceptance: Pending and done lists contain only business navigation actions
counterexample: Task center shows approve, reject or return controls

requirements.statement: Workflow management contains definitions and monitoring only.
acceptance: Inbox and done menus are absent
WorkflowView exposes no business approval action
counterexample: Workflow menu still contains pending approval

requirements.statement: The workflow platform exposes current-user task context for business pages.
acceptance: Single-task response includes business route, node, status, allowed actions, signature requirement and actionable result
counterexample: Business page scans the entire inbox to infer task permission

requirements.statement: Task context and decisions enforce authorization and state on the server.
acceptance: Wrong assignee, completed, missing and duplicate actions are rejected
counterexample: Changing taskId in the URL exposes approval capability

requirements.statement: A successful decision refreshes the current business page in place.
acceptance: Application status, workflow progress and audit log update without navigating away
counterexample: Approval redirects to a generic workflow list

acceptance: Old inbox and done routes reach task center
Old review route reaches business detail when possible or dashboard otherwise
counterexample: An old task link renders a blank or generic approval page

requirements.statement: Workflow inbox and done menus are removed by a forward migration while APIs remain.
acceptance: Menus 202 and 204 and their role links are absent after migration
Inbox, done and decision endpoints remain available
counterexample: Existing Flyway files are edited or task APIs are deleted

requirements.statement: Business-owned approval is responsive on desktop and required phone viewports.
acceptance: Complete form and permitted actions remain reachable at 1280x800, 375x812, 390x844 and 430x932
counterexample: Mobile users must horizontally scroll the page to approve

invariants: Release management owns release business data and rendering
Workflow owns task state, assignee, allowed actions, signatures and audit
Workbench surfaces never duplicate business approval forms
Frontend visibility never replaces server authorization
A workflow action path is an internal absolute business path
constraints: Current release data remains a replaceable Mock Provider
Preserve existing workflow inbox, done, decision and monitoring APIs
Use Vue 3, TypeScript, Element Plus and existing dependencies
Use a new V37 forward migration for menu removal
Meet desktop and 375x812, 390x844 and 430x932 acceptance viewports
non_goals: Business DTO rendering inside workflow management
Quick approval from dashboard or task center
Deleting workflow task projection or decision APIs

selected_approach.name: Business-owned release detail route with embedded approval panel
selected_approach.reason: It preserves complete decision context, stable deep links and clear ownership while reusing platform task authorization and decision services.

alternatives.name: Query-driven detail drawer
alternatives.rejected_because: Refresh, browser history, deep links and long mobile content remain weak.

alternatives.name: Workflow dynamically hosts business components
alternatives.rejected_because: Workflow would continue owning business presentation and create cross-module coupling.

inside: release business detail and approval panel
workflow menu removal and route compatibility
outside: project, subsystem, delivery-unit and requirement integrations

components.name: ReleaseApplicationDetailPage
components.responsibility: Render full release application, workflow progress and conditional approval UI

components.name: ReleaseApprovalPanel
components.responsibility: Collect comment, current-login signature and permitted decision

components.name: TaskCenterView
components.responsibility: Paginate pending and done projections and navigate to business paths

components.name: WorkflowView
components.responsibility: Manage definitions and monitor instances only

components.name: WorkflowTaskContext
components.responsibility: Project a single task and current-user action capability
depends_on: workflow task, instance, signature configuration and authentication

components.name: V37 menu migration
components.responsibility: Remove inbox and done menu entries and role links

interfaces.name: workflow_task_context
interfaces.contract: Returns current-user task status, business context, actions, signature requirement and actionable flag

interfaces.name: workflow_task_decision
interfaces.contract: Server-authorized decision using current login identity and existing audit/signature behavior

interfaces.name: workflow_task_projection
interfaces.contract: Pending and done rows include stable business_key and safe action_path

data_flows.output: updated read-only or next-node business detail

transitions: load release application and workflow history

error_handling.condition: Business application is missing or fails to load
error_handling.behavior: Do not render approval controls; show explicit business error
error_handling.recovery: Retry or return to application/task list

error_handling.condition: Task is missing, completed or stale
error_handling.behavior: Keep business detail and show read-only stale-task state

error_handling.condition: Current user is not the assignee
error_handling.behavior: Do not expose action capability and reject decisions with 403
error_handling.recovery: Return to task center or use authorized identity

error_handling.behavior: Preserve entered comment and report conflict without local success mutation
error_handling.recovery: Reload context and decide again if still allowed

error_handling.condition: Historical action path cannot identify release business
error_handling.recovery: Locate the task from task center

security: Server validates tenant, assignee, task state, action and current-login signature
Business detail must load before approval
action_path remains an internal absolute path
performance: Dashboard loads five items per group
Business page queries one task rather than scanning inbox
compatibility: Inbox, done and decision APIs remain
Menu rollback uses a new forward migration
operations: Workflow monitor remains the technical audit surface
Log stale-task, denied-decision and route-conversion failures

verification_strategy.signal: All entry points reach one responsive business page and permitted actions complete in place
verification_strategy.method: Desktop and three-phone browser interaction including refresh, back and stale task

verification_strategy.signal: Workflow menu and page expose definitions and monitoring only
verification_strategy.method: Flyway data assertion, fresh login navigation and route checks

verification_strategy.signal: Single-task context and decisions distinguish valid, denied, completed and missing tasks
verification_strategy.method: Workflow module Java tests and HTTP integration checks

verification_strategy.signal: Repository and integration regressions are absent
verification_strategy.method: Java 17 Maven tests, frontend build, governance, Flyway and diff checks

assumptions.text: Workflow business_key equals the stable release application code
assumptions.basis: Existing business integration contract and tests use business keys and release action paths
assumptions.falsifier: Formal release API uses an unrelated mutable identifier

assumptions.text: Existing workflow decision and signature semantics can be reused unchanged
assumptions.basis: Current service validates pending tasks and current-login signature
assumptions.falsifier: Business-owned UI requires an action not represented by the published workflow action contract

assumptions.text: Current release mock provider can resolve applicationCode across the business route
assumptions.basis: Mock applications already have unique code fields
assumptions.falsifier: Route refresh cannot recreate the selected application from deterministic state

unknowns.question: When will the formal release detail API replace the mock provider?
unknowns.impact: Durable cross-session approval state remains unproven

unknowns.question: When will notifications expose the same action_path navigation?
unknowns.impact: Notification acceptance remains a later integration check

decisions.decision: Use an independent business-owned release detail route
decisions.reason: Stable deep links and complete decision context

decisions.decision: Remove workflow inbox and done menus
decisions.reason: Workflow management is configuration and monitoring only
Prevents a second generic approval surface

decisions.decision: Keep task authorization, signature and decision in workflow backend
decisions.reason: Preserves platform security and audit ownership

decisions.decision: Keep release business data behind a mock provider for this implementation
decisions.reason: Formal owning modules are not yet available

risks.risk: Historical action paths point to old workflow pages
risks.impact: Tasks fail to reach business context
risks.mitigation: Provide route compatibility and safe business-path conversion

risks.impact: Prototype decisions can appear inconsistent after navigation
risks.mitigation: Use a shared deterministic session repository and disclose non-persistence

risks.risk: Single-task context leaks another user's task
risks.mitigation: Filter by tenant and current user and repeat all checks at decision time
Keep redirect routes and restore menus only by a forward migration if rolled back

approval.evidence: User confirmed removing workflow inbox/done, selected option 1, and approved the user-flow, architecture/interface, page-state and acceptance sections.
